title: AssetInventory
description: Agent B's (Archive/Visual Editor) B-DISCOVER output: real discovered assets plus beat-level coverage planning against producer_outline.json. Central rule: DISCOVERY IS NOT VERIFICATION -- finding a plausible search result is not the same as having looked at the thing. Coverage is beat-centric: beat_coverage[].target_visual_sec is copied directly from producer_outline.json's beat.estimated_narration_sec (Agent B's visual workload budget for that beat), not a per-visual_request checklist -- visual_requests remain advisory search hints only. A single long source video may contain multiple non-contiguous useful regions; each is recorded as its own usable_segments[] entry rather than one start/end pair per asset -- see agents/agent_b_archive_visual_editor.md.

status.description: pending: Agent B has not run. gathered: every producer_outline.json beat has exactly one beat_coverage entry, none is critical_gap, and overall_effective_coverage (see agents/agent_a_producer_writer.md's A-FINAL gate) is >= 0.90. approved: reviewed. Agent A's A4 stage is gated on this reaching gathered or approved.

environment_limitations.description: Capabilities this run genuinely lacked, stated plainly rather than hidden -- e.g. 'cannot decode video frames, so no video asset can exceed verification_method: metadata_only', or 'domain X blocks this crawler'. A limitation recorded here is the justification for weaker verification_method values elsewhere in the file.

assets.description: Every real asset discovered, regardless of which beat(s) use it. The same asset may be allocated to multiple beats via beat_coverage[].allocations -- store it once here. Downloading the source file never trims or overwrites it: usable_segments records permitted RANGES within the intact original, it does not cut it.

source_url.description: Where the asset lives. At least one of source_url or local_path must be present (enforced above) -- an asset with neither is not a discovered asset. Prefer having both once downloaded.

source_title.description: Title of the page, archive record, or publication the asset came from -- so a later reviewer can retrace the find

description.description: What the asset actually shows. If verification_method is not visually_inspected, this describes what the SOURCE CLAIMS it shows -- say so.

exact_subject_match.description: Whether this asset genuinely shows the exact subject requested. MUST NOT be set true unless verification_method is visually_inspected. A title, filename, caption, search snippet, or metadata field is never sufficient evidence that an image or video depicts a specific model year or variant. Any allocation using this asset with relevance: exact requires this to be true.

access_status.description: How much of the source was actually reached, mirroring fact_pack.json's source access semantics

verification_method.description: How the asset's CONTENT was established. visually_inspected: the image, or the relevant video frames, were actually viewed (e.g. via scripts/media_probe.py's contact sheets). metadata_only: title/caption/EXIF/archive record read, content not viewed. search_result_only: known only from a search listing. unverified: neither content nor metadata confirmed. usable_segments may only be non-empty when this is visually_inspected.

duration_sec.description: Video only (required when asset_type is video). Total source duration, e.g. from scripts/media_probe.py's probe(). Used to bound usable_segments -- a segment's end_sec must not exceed this.

usable_segments.description: Video only. A source video may contain several useful, non-contiguous regions -- one entry per region, rather than a single asset-wide start/end. Only allowed when verification_method is visually_inspected; empty or absent otherwise. Never invent timestamps from a title, description, or search result.

segment_id.description: Unique across the ENTIRE asset_inventory.json (not just within this asset), e.g. 'asset_014_s1'. Referenced by beat_coverage[].allocations[].segment_id and later by edit_plan.json clips.

end_sec.description: Must exceed start_sec, and must not exceed the asset's duration_sec when known.

visual_quality.description: Use unknown unless the asset was actually viewed

license.description: Licence/rights status if known, or an explicit note that it is unknown

reusable.description: Whether this asset (or its segments) is generic/flexible enough to reasonably allocate to more than one beat (e.g. a contextual factory shot or a period logo), as opposed to something that only makes sense for the one beat it was found for.

beat_coverage.description: PRIMARY coverage contract. Exactly one entry per beat in producer_outline.json's beats array -- a beat with no entry, or more than one entry, is an error. target_visual_sec must equal the outline beat's estimated_narration_sec when the outline provides one.

act.description: Optional. Mirrors the beat's act in producer_outline.json when the channel uses an act_structure. Not required.

target_visual_sec.description: The visual workload budget for this beat. MUST equal producer_outline.json's beat.estimated_narration_sec when the outline provides one -- Agent B may not lower this to make coverage easier. Only when the outline beat genuinely has no estimated_narration_sec may Agent B set its own reasonable value, and it must then explain the fallback in notes.

planned_visual_sec.description: MUST equal the sum of this entry's allocations[].planned_sec (within rounding tolerance) -- not a number claimed independently of the allocations that back it.

coverage_ratio.description: planned_visual_sec / target_visual_sec. Deterministic -- must equal that division (within rounding). If target_visual_sec is 0, set this to 1.0 and explain in notes.

coverage_status.description: V0 planning thresholds against coverage_ratio: sufficient >= 0.90, partial >= 0.60 and < 0.90, critical_gap < 0.60. Simple planning guidance, not a scoring system. Per-beat status alone does not open the A-FINAL gate -- see agents/agent_a_producer_writer.md for the episode-level overall_effective_coverage requirement.

allocations.description: Assets (and, for video, specific usable_segments) planned for this beat's screen time. May be empty only if coverage_status is critical_gap.

asset_id.description: References an asset_id in this file's assets array. The same asset_id may appear in multiple beats' allocations.

segment_id.description: Video assets only, and required for them: references one of that asset's usable_segments[].segment_id. Absent for photo/document/etc. assets, which have no segments. Different segments of the same video asset may serve different beats (even different acts) -- that's expected, not a problem.

planned_sec.description: Approximate planned screen time for this asset within this beat. For a video allocation this must not exceed the referenced segment's own duration (end_sec - start_sec) -- only the selected usable material counts, never the source video's full runtime. Soft editorial guidance (not a hard validation limit) for typical values: ~15-35s for a good relevant video segment or ~15-30s contextual video, ~8-18s photo, ~10-20s brochure/document/magazine, ~8-15s map/chart. Longer is fine when genuinely appropriate -- don't mechanically chop a strong clip just to fit a range.

relevance.description: exact: the exact vehicle/object/event being discussed -- requires the referenced asset's exact_subject_match to be true. adjacent: a closely related model, sibling vehicle, factory, company, component, or same project. contextual: period/geography/industry footage supporting the narration without claiming to depict the exact subject. documentary_fallback: brochure, document, advertisement, magazine scan, map, chart, archive still, etc. A beat is not required to have exact-relevance material for every second -- a coherent visual story matters more than exactness for every allocation.

request_coverage.description: OPTIONAL, secondary traceability only -- NOT the completion gate. beat_coverage is the primary contract; a visual_request with no entry here is not a gap by itself as long as its beat's coverage is sufficient/partial. Use this only when per-request traceability is genuinely useful (e.g. auditing which specific request a high-priority exact asset satisfies).

request_id.description: References a visual_request request_id from producer_outline.json

coverage_status.description: found_exact / found_partial / context_only MUST each reference at least one real asset_id in asset_ids. not_found MUST have an empty asset_ids array. found_exact additionally requires that at least one referenced asset has exact_subject_match: true.

asset_ids.description: asset_id values in this file that address the request. Empty if and only if coverage_status is not_found.

search_attempts.description: What was actually searched, if recorded.
